reason: Conversation 1 handled the critical safety stop more completely: it ordered the steps correctly (don't touch plug/machine, isolate at the consumer unit from the dry hall, then turn off the water supply), addressed the wet-socks slip and shock risk, told her to drain the drum via the filter before opening the door, and correctly narrowed the front leak to the door seal after the filter cap checked out. Conversation 2 got the isolation right and did reach the confirmed seal-tear diagnosis and model number, but it never told her to shut off the water, told her to open the door with a drum still full of water, gave a confusing non-answer about the socket mid-conversation, and its final part card offered a £5 clamp band rather than the door seal it had just said she needed. C1 gave no incorrect advice and escalated appropriately (electrician if the socket got wet, engineer or Beko for the seal), so it served her better despite not finishing the diagnosis.
